title: Placing Grid Items 🧩
description: Position items on the grid using line numbers, `span`, named lines, and the `grid-area` shorthand.

slides.title: Grid Lines: The Coordinates 📍
slides.content:
# Numbered From 1 (and -1)

Every grid has numbered grid lines. By default, items auto‑place (flowing into the next available cell). You can override this by explicitly placing items on the grid using `grid-column` and `grid-row`.

- `grid-column-start`, `grid-column-end`
- `grid-row-start`, `grid-row-end`
- Shorthands: `grid-column` (start / end), `grid-row` (start / end)

```css
.item {
  grid-column: 1 / 3;  /* span from line 1 to line 3 (occupies columns 1 and 2) */
  grid-row: 2 / 4;
}
```
Negative line numbers count from the end: -1 is the last line.

slides.title: The `span` Keyword 🌉
slides.content:
# Span a Number of Tracks

Instead of specifying exact end lines, you can use `span`:
```css
.item {
  grid-column: 1 / span 2; /* start at line 1, span 2 columns */
  grid-row: span 3; /* start auto‑placed, span 3 rows */
}
```
`span` is helpful when you don't know the exact line numbers, or when items are auto‑placed and you want them to occupy a certain width.

quizData.question: What does `grid-column: 2 / span 2;` do?

options.text: Starts at line 2 and ends at line 2
Starts at line 2 and spans 2 columns (lines 2 to 4)

quizData.explanation: `2 / span 2` means start at line 2 and extend across two column tracks, ending at line 4.

slides.title: Named Grid Lines 🏷️
The `grid-area` Shorthand (Line‑Based) 📦
An Overlapping Layout
slides.content: Grid allows intentional overlaps for creative designs:

quizData.question: The `grid-area` shorthand takes four values in the order: ______.
quizData.explanation: Grid‑area order is row-start, column-start, row-end, column-end.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Visualise with DevTools

Activate the grid overlay in Firefox or Chrome DevTools. Hover over items to see their line placement. It makes understanding explicit placement trivial.
